column1: # Regex feature conformance corpus for issue #104 (two-phase-regex article).
#   pattern = raw regex body. The harness wraps it in /.../ for the engine
#             (StepLexer token-rule syntax) and in \A(?:...) for the .NET
#             Regex reference, so both engines answer "does this pattern
#             match at position 0 of the input, and what is the match?".
#   input   = literal text; the escapes \\ \n \t are decoded by the harness.
#   feature = tag used for per-feature pass-rate aggregation.
# A case passes when the engine compiles the pattern AND its observable
# result (matched / not matched / matched text) equals the .NET reference.
# Zero-width reference matches count as pass iff the engine does not match
# (the engine rejects zero-width matches by design, issue #111).
# are rejected by the engine at compile time on purpose (token-rule patterns
# are forward-only NFAs); the suite pins that rejection and reports these
# features as 0% support vs .NET Regex, which is the "unsupported features
# must be listed" outcome the article needs.
# quantifier-lazy and alternation-order are measured without a 100% floor:
# the engine never backtracks (lazy = exactly the minimum; alternation =
# longest match), which can diverge from .NET's leftmost-first backtracking.
